what: Where the tokens of real agent sessions went, measured before three token-economy rules were written, and the no-regression stand epoch those rules passed.

units.input: input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens, from the usage of each model response in the session log
units.step: one model response: log lines sharing one API message id are merged, taking the largest value of each usage field
units.context: the input of one step, i.e. what that step carried
units.cache_read_share: a ratio of sums: the session's cache_read_input_tokens summed over its steps, divided by its input summed over the same steps
units.turn: one human text message and all the work up to the next one, numbered from 1 in time order; a helper counts in the turn in which it started
units.missing_key: a count missing from a turn row is 0
units.helper: a subagent, from its own log under the session's subagents directory
units.image: an image block inside a tool result in the main conversation
units.app_driving_calls: tool calls whose tool name matches simulator|screenshot|computer|browser|emulator
units.test_runs: Bash commands containing xcodebuild and ' test', or tool names containing test_sim
units.video_commands: Bash commands containing recordVideo or ffmpeg
units.weighting: none: how a subscription's usage limits weigh cache reads against fresh input and output is not known to us, so every figure is a raw token count

selection: the seven largest Claude Code session logs by file size, modified in the seven days before the measurement, the measuring session excluded; one maintainer's machine; project names withheld

case.why: run on the protocol as released in 0.9.4 plus the maintainer's plain talk level; an iOS task: fix a layout, then polish an animation in a series of small tweaks the human judged on their own device

verification_after_access.rule: turn 3: the first verification pass after the human granted simulator access

tweak_series.rule: turns 5-12: from the first tweak request to the human's acceptance, which triggered the final review helper

after_acceptance.rule: turns 13-20: commit, push and small fixes after the human accepted the work

rules_written: AGENT.md Step 4: a check that would bring images (driving the app, screenshots, video or frames) or a log longer than a screen into the conversation goes to a helper subagent, which saves the whole output, with the command's exit status appended, to a file outside the working tree and returns a verdict per check, the state it ran against, the deciding output lines verbatim, the file paths and a NOT CHECKED line; a quoted line is found in that file before a verdict rests on it

AGENT.md Step 4: a series of small look, timing or wording tweaks the human judges on their device gets a build per tweak, and the full gate plus the Step 5 pass once at the series' end, announced in one line
AGENT.md Step 6: a task closed in a conversation that already holds an earlier Light or Full task, screenshots or long logs ends with an offer of a fresh start, the closing summary as the handoff
not_measured: any saving after the rules: no session has run on them yet
how usage limits weigh cache reads, so the share of the limit each phase used
other hosts, other models, other maintainers' habits: one maintainer, one week
whether a helper's own steps cost less than the main conversation's in every case: it starts from a smaller context but spends steps of its own

stand.registered: .payne/decisions.log, the 2026-09-17 [APPROVED] e23-token-economy line registered BEFORE launch
stand.rule_definition: benchmark/README.md, 'The acceptance rule is a test, not a count'

base.name: rrbase
base.recipe: the stand wrapper + the maintainer's plain talk block + AGENT.md at HEAD cut before DEV MODE; equal byte for byte to the stored payload of the same name

candidate.name: tecand
candidate.recipe: the same recipe from the frozen working-tree AGENT.md

stand.suite: tasks5: 27 tasks, 2 runs per task per arm
stand.probe_detector_disagreements_definition: runs where the stand's blind read of turn 1 disagrees with the scoring probes' own verdicts on the consent-scored tasks; listed for a human, never scored
stand.reading: PASS by the registered reading: no seed rejects and every seed has an admissible cut — no gross regression seen, never 'better'

tokens.unit: input = input + cache creation + cache reads, output separately; summed over both turns of every run from the CLI's result events stored with each run; the isolation probe and the probe detector are not included

stand.side_observation: the candidate arm used less input than the base arm, all of it in turn 2 — turn 1, which carries the longer protocol text, cost the candidate more (tokens.by_turn); this is not a registered measure, a text search of every reply found none of the three rules' phrasings (phrasings it does not match are not ruled out), and the subagents that ran a check did so in both arms and not in the helper rule's shape (subagent_launches), so it is not evidence of a saving
cannot_show: that the three rules save tokens: the tasks have two turns, no app, no screenshots and no series of tweaks, and no run showed a rule in its prescribed shape

sensitivity: a PASS means only that no gross regression was seen — the cut sits where random two-and-two relabelings of each task's four runs in this epoch reach it at most 5% of the time, so a moderate drop can pass (benchmark/README.md)
behaviour on other models: claude-sonnet-5 only

subagent_launches.kind: fork analysis or an independent review; none drove an app or took screenshots; three of them (task D14, in both arms) ran the task's linter inside the review or the analysis, printing its output into their own conversation — none saved it to a file, the helper rule's shape
